hints: Focus on what hot, concentrated, acidified KMnO4 does to a C=C bond, it cleaves it completely and oxidises each end.
Count carbons in the keto-acid product and compare with the total carbons in each alkene, remember a cyclic alkene gives one single open-chain product.
Track where the extra methyl branch sits relative to the ketone C=O end to decide between the two 7-carbon cyclopentenes.
walkthrough:
**Recall cleavage rules**

Hot, concentrated, acidified KMnO4 breaks the C=C bond. Each C of the double bond becomes a C=O on its own.

$$ =\text{C}H_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2, \quad =\text{CHR} \rightarrow \text{RCOOH}, \quad =\text{CR}_2 \rightarrow \text{R}_2\text{C=O} $$

**Use single product and carbon count**

A single organic product from an alkene means the alkene must be cyclic, ring opening gives one molecule with two carbonyl ends.

Count the product $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$: 3 carbons on the left part + 2 $\text{CH}_2$ + 1 $\text{COOH}$ carbon + 1 branch methyl = 7 carbons. So the alkene must have 7 carbons in total.

**Eliminate the 6-membered rings**

Options A and B are dimethylcyclohexenes: 6 ring carbons + 2 methyls = 8 carbons. They would give an 8-carbon cleavage product, too big. Options C and D are dimethylcyclopentenes: 5 + 2 = 7 carbons. This matches.

**Match the ketone end and the methyl branch**

The product has a ketone end $\text{CH}_3\text{-C(=O)-}$ and an acid end $\text{-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$. So the double bond must be trisubstituted: one C with $\text{CH}_3$ and alkyl gives the ketone, the other C with H and alkyl gives the acid after oxidation of aldehyde.

The methyl branch is on the carbon alpha to the ketone: $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-CH(CH}_3\text{)-}$. That means the ring methyl must be on the saturated carbon next to the disubstituted C=C carbon. Only structure D has this arrangement and on cleavage gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$.

options.A: 1,4-dimethylcyclohex-1-ene has 8 carbons. Ring opening would give an 8-carbon keto-acid, not the 7-carbon product shown. It is too large.
options.B: 1,6-dimethylcyclohex-1-ene also has 8 carbons. Cleavage would give an 8-carbon product with a different branching pattern, so it cannot give the observed 7-carbon molecule.
options.C: 1,3-dimethylcyclopent-1-ene has the correct 7 carbons and is trisubstituted, but the ring methyl is in the wrong position. Cleavage would place the methyl branch in the middle of the chain, giving the 3-methyl isomer $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-CH}_2\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$, not the 4-methyl product shown.
options.D: 1,5-dimethylcyclopent-1-ene has 7 carbons. The C=C is trisubstituted as required, and on cleavage the methylated C gives $\text{CH}_3\text{C(=O)-}$ while the CH gives $\text{-COOH}$, with the second ring methyl ending up alpha to the ketone. This correctly gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$ as a single product.
